newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Outsiders Lead World Cities Chess meet in Indonesi.
newsitem.headline: Outsiders Lead World Cities Chess meet in Indonesi.

text.p: Seven teams lead the inaugural World Cities Chess Championship in Jakarta after top seeds stumbled in the first round on Tuesday.
Of the favourites, only Oslo remains on a perfect score of four points after the first day of the event.
Top seeds Moscow and Donetsk trail the leaders by half a point after their top players, Alexander Onischuk and Igor Novikov respectively, were held to draws by lowly ranked opponents.

Despite their first round set-back, the all-Grandmaster Russian line-up is expected to dominate a competition weakened by what the organisers allege was a concerted effort by the World Chess Federation, FIDE, to undermine the event.
The first World Cities Championship has attracted 28 teams from 13 countries, including 17 Grandmasters, but many more were expected.
"We lost many cities through last-minute withdrawals," said event spokesman Max Wotulo. "I don't know what FIDE think they are doing -- we are just trying to organise a new chess event," he added.
The President of the Philippines Chess Federation, Arturo Borjal, said high level pressure had been exerted to prevent the top Filipino players from taking part in the Jakarta tournament.

Speaking from Manila shortly before the event began, Borjal said "I don't know if this is sabotage or not, but the players told me that they had been warned by Campo Filipino FIDE Chairman Florencio Campomanes that if they played in the World Cities they would be banned from the FIDE World Teams Championship later this year."
The Philippines has sent only a second-string team from the city of Mandaluyung, a team which is surprisingly among the early leaders.
The World Cities Championship continues tomorrow and concludes on July 14. Gunadarma World Cities Championship, Jakarta Results of Round 1:

1.eq Oslo (NOR), Ho Chi Minh (VIE), Mandaluyung (PHI), Depok Kelapa (INA), Depok Bji (INA), Jakarta A (INA), Jakarta B (INA) 4; Moscow (RUS), Donetsk (UKR), Bandung (INA) 3.5; Tashkent (UZB) Depok Margonda (INA) 3; Sydney (AUS), Ambon (INA) 2.5; Bontang (INA), Jakarta Women (INA) 1.5; Medan (INA), Yogyakarta (INA) 1; Rangoon (BRM), Kuala Lumpur (MAS), Mandalay (BRM) 0.5; Raffles City (SIP), Hong Kong (CHI), Victoria (SEY), Sentosa (SIP), Kuching (MAS), Noumea (NCA), Jakarta C (INA) 0.
